dissents.topic: Whether _process_messages should have been folded into _receive_messages

positions.position: The split into _process_messages (filter) and _receive_messages (error boundary) was the right Unix-style decomposition; the fix should subtract the bug (the swallowing try/except) not the structure. Collapsing them is the wrong cut.

Keep the two concerns separate: _receive_messages drives the async-for and logs 'stream ended, will reconnect'; _process_messages stays a pure parse-and-dispatch step. The bug was the broad try/except, not the existence of the inner method.

Does not call for restoring the split, but flags that the lost 'WebSocket connection closed' diagnostic and the new method's implicit termination contract need a literate comment or restored try/except + log.
Endorses the collapse — deleting the swallowing except is GOOD-TASTE; the special case did nothing useful and removing it makes control flow obvious. No objection to the merged structure.

Does not object to the merge per se, but flags that the supertype contract with the outer reconnect loop is now implicit and undocumented; either restore the outer try/except with diagnostic log or document the propagation behavior.
Does not object to the merge, but says the fix is at the wrong altitude — the real locus of the bug is the outer reconnect loop in websocket_service.py, which is not audited in this PR.

dissents.topic: Severity of the duplicate 'transcriber_error' tuple entry

positions.position: P1 — readability defect; reader will pause to ask whether duplication is meaningful.
P1 — symptom that the set of error kinds is data complected with control flow; should be a frozenset value.
P1 — either careless copy-paste or a typo for a different string; maintainer will waste time on it.
P1 — a tell that the data structure is wrong; tuple-of-strings doing set work.
P1 — direct evidence the set was assembled by enumeration without checking against the specification.
P2 — harmless at runtime; signals the list was assembled without a spec check but does not rise to a should-fix-before-merge.

dissents.topic: Whether the inner bare-except Exception inside the async-for is a problem

positions.position: P1 — DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for reasoning about message shape; same anti-pattern that produced the original infinite-loop bug at smaller scale; should be replaced with explicit reasoning about which exceptions _process_response is permitted to raise.
P2 — swallows everything including programmer errors; complects 'their payload was weird' with 'our code has a bug'.

Treats it as an open contract question — notes connection-level exceptions from the async iterator now propagate where the inner except only covers JSON decode and processing errors; asks for explicit documentation.
Does not flag the inner bare except as an issue.
Does not flag the inner bare except as an issue.
Does not flag the inner bare except as a distinct issue beyond the implicit-contract concern.

issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' string in the error message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple of error message types contains 'transcriber_error' twice. Harmless at runtime (membership is idempotent), but it is direct evidence the set was assembled by copy-paste rather than checked against the ElevenLabs specification. All six reviewers flagged it; the fix is to deduplicate and promote the catalog to a named module-level frozenset (e.g., ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES) with a docs link.

issues.description: Per-error-type log context dropped: logger.error calls and category prefixes lost in consolidation
issues.detail: Previously auth_error / quota_exceeded_error produced distinct logger.error lines ('ElevenLabs auth error: ...', 'ElevenLabs quota exceeded: ...') and labeled push_error prefixes ('Auth error: ...', 'Quota exceeded: ...'). The new unified branch emits only a generic 'Error: {error_msg}' with no logger.error at all. Operators relying on logs to triage ElevenLabs auth/quota failures lose both the explicit log line and the typed categorization on the pushed frame. Restore logger.error(f'ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}') and include message_type in the push_error string, or use a dispatch table {message_type: (log_level, prefix)}.

issues.description: Lost 'WebSocket connection closed' diagnostic and implicit termination contract of _receive_messages
issues.detail: The previous _receive_messages wrapped _process_messages in try/except and logged 'WebSocket connection closed: {e}' before returning, giving operators a clear breadcrumb that the outer reconnect loop was about to act. After the refactor that diagnostic is gone, and the method's precondition / postcondition / termination behavior (what exceptions propagate vs. are swallowed, what the contract with the outer reconnect loop in websocket_service.py is) is implicit. Either restore the outer try/except + log line, or add a docstring stating the contract so the next maintainer does not reintroduce the swallowing except.

issues.description: _process_messages folded into _receive_messages — separation of concerns lost
issues.detail: The previous decomposition cleanly split a per-message parse-and-dispatch filter (_process_messages) from a lifecycle/error boundary (_receive_messages). The PR collapsed them to fix the swallowing-except bug, but the bug was the broad try/except itself, not the existence of two functions. Keep the split: _receive_messages drives the async-for and logs 'stream ended, will reconnect'; _process_messages remains a stateless transform. Subtract the bug, not the structure.

issues.description: Error-type set is data complected with control flow; needs a named module-level constant with spec link
issues.detail: The catalog of fourteen error message_types lives inline in an elif branch as a tuple literal. The set of known error kinds is documentation-derived data about the ElevenLabs API, not control flow. It should be a module-level named constant (frozenset or dict mapping message_type -> human prefix / log level) with a docstring linking to the ElevenLabs error-handling docs, so the precondition is explicit, drift from upstream docs is auditable, and the duplicate-key class of bug is impossible by construction.

issues.description: Inner bare 'except Exception' inside per-message loop is the same anti-pattern as the bug being fixed
issues.detail: The remaining try/except inside the async-for catches json.JSONDecodeError (reasonable) and then bare Exception, logging and continuing. This is precisely the defensive-programming construct that produced the original infinite-loop bug at a smaller scale: arbitrary failures in _process_response (KeyError, attribute errors, half-broken connection state, programmer errors) are converted to a log line and the loop continues forever. State which exceptions _process_response is permitted to raise under a well-formed message and let everything else propagate; or distinguish 'their payload was weird' from 'our code has a bug' explicitly.

issues.description: Outer reconnect loop in websocket_service.py is the real locus of the invariant and is not audited in this PR
issues.detail: The fix correctly removes the swallowing except so disconnects propagate, but it relies on the outer loop in websocket_service.py (lines 133-154) to reconnect-or-exit correctly. That loop's invariant ('on transient failure, reconnect with bounded backoff; on permanent failure, exit') is not stated or verified in this diff. If the outer loop also catches Exception and retries without backoff, the infinite loop merely moves up one frame. Confirm the outer loop has bounded retry / exponential backoff / a termination condition.

issues.description: push_error contract for ErrorFrame vs. string not verified
issues.detail: The PR description says 'Add error frame for all error types' but the call passes error_msg=f'...' as a keyword argument. If push_error's signature expects an ErrorFrame instance, this is wrong; if it accepts a string and wraps it, fine — but the diff does not show enough context to confirm. Not a regression (pre-existing code did the same), but worth verifying the contract instead of assuming.

changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a newline ('\ No newline at end of file'). POSIX text-file convention and most concatenation tooling expect a trailing newline; tools that join changelog fragments will run lines together. One-byte fix.

issues.description: Default error string for unknown_error fallback regressed in human readability
issues.detail: data.get('error', f'Unknown error - {message_type}') yields strings like 'Unknown error - quota_exceeded_error' which read worse than the prior per-branch defaults like 'Quota exceeded'. Acceptable tradeoff for the consolidation, but a minor regression in human-readable error text.

issues.description: PR squashes two unrelated changes (reconnect fix + error-type expansion) into one patch
issues.detail: Patch 1: remove the swallowing try/except so the outer reconnect loop sees disconnects. Patch 2: expand the error message_type list. They are unrelated concerns; squashing them makes git bisect worse and review harder. Not a blocker on a small PR, but worth noting.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR correctly diagnoses a real bug — an inner try/except around _process_messages converted websocket disconnects into a silently-swallowed exception, which the outer reconnect loop then spun on — and that removing the swallowing wrapper is the right structural move. All six reviewers independently flagged the duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry, the loss of per-error-type logger.error context and typed push_error prefixes, the missing trailing newline in the changelog, and (in five of six) the absence of a named module-level constant for the error-type catalog. The strongest preserved disagreement is structural: Pike and Hickey argue the fix went too far by folding _process_messages back into _receive_messages — the bug was the broad try/except, not the two-function decomposition — while Torvalds explicitly praises the collapse as GOOD-TASTE and Dijkstra/Liskov are agnostic on the merge but want the new method's contract documented. Dijkstra alone notes the actual invariant lives in websocket_service.py's outer reconnect loop, which this PR does not audit; if that loop also catches Exception without backoff, the infinite-loop merely moves up one frame. Verdict across the panel: real bug, right direction, but TESTED-NOT-PROVED — fix the duplicate, name the constant, restore the per-type log context, document the contract, and confirm the outer loop's termination.
